The lavaan::growth() function is a wrapper for the lavaan::lavaan() function. It takes pretty much the same arguments, so use ordered =[ordered vars] and estimator = [your favorite estimator - probably wlsmv].

Depending on exactly what you want to do, it can be easier and equivalent using lme4::glmer() - at least you sometimes need to write a lot less code.


On Sun, Dec 8, 2024, 8:23 AM Mitch <mitch.s...@gmail.com> wrote:

I am specifying a latent longitudinal growth curve model in R with multiple time-invariant covariates. However, my outcome is binary (0/1). I read through the growth() function documentation, but didn't find anything specific to my situation. I know it's statistically possible, but was wondering if anything needs to be done with syntax to account for the outcome.

Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: Binary Outcome with Growth Curve Model
parts:
my outcome is binary (0/1)... I know it's statistically possible

Not really.  With only 1 threshold, any change in (latent-response) means is perfectly confounded with any change in (latent-response) variance.  You need at least 2 thresholds to disentangle those 2 types of change.
